```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Reaching a first payment within 90 days depends on who pays. In A, one buyer pays: an engineering team lead buying per-seat. In B, revenue mostly arrives as a success fee at close, so the operator needs both sellers and active buyers and then a completed deal, all inside 90 days.",
    "B's own brief documents its main failure mode with sourced evidence. The closest comparable (DealMyApp) reports traffic and listings but weak buyer conversion two weeks after launch. A $750 newsletter test aimed at a similar audience produced 124 clicks and zero sales.",
    "B cannot compete on price. Three of its five live competitors charge 0% or near-0% commission, so sellers have free alternatives, which undercuts listing-fee revenue as a fallback.",
    "A has a sourced, replicable monetization anchor: Lody's $8–10/seat/month for the workspace layer alone, with no markup on model usage. That suggests a small team could pay for collaboration without a governance-heavy enterprise deal.",
    "A is also crowded, and Slack Code is free. But a crowded single-sided SaaS market still allows one niche team to become a paying customer. A cold-start two-sided marketplace usually cannot produce a closed deal in that window."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's 'Case For' rests on the claim that AI agents can replicate Acquire.com's human acquisition-expert services (listing optimization, buyer vetting, deal coaching) at near-zero cost and out-service incumbents in sub-$10k deals. Nothing in the brief shows this is feasible or that buyers or sellers would value or pay for it. The cited source only shows that Acquire.com offers these services. The seller-side demand quote ('I didn't know where serious buyers were') points to buyer liquidity as the real gap, which agent-delivered services do not address.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. A wins mainly because B's two-sided cold-start problem is well documented against a 90-day target, not because A's case is strong. A's demand evidence is two anecdotal quotes about agent visibility, not willingness to pay for multiplayer control. The YC Fall 2026 RFS is mentioned without a source. Both six-week buildability and non-engineering demand are marked [unsourced]. Slack Code sets a $0 anchor, and the security/governance bar (SOC2, SSO, ZDR) may block adoption. If those A risks hold, both ideas could fail to land a paying customer in 90 days."
}
```
